end.summary:
Identified common non-metals and their states; this was shown on a new-situation question.
Explained the roles of oxygen, carbon and nitrogen in living things; this was shown on a why question.
Practised everyday uses of non-metals, including graphite, chlorine, iodised salt, fertilisers, rocket fuel, balloons and nitrogen in snack packets.
Used examples and cause-and-effect reasoning, such as nitrogen preventing staleness and protecting chips from breaking.
end.parentNote: Pari practised the uses and states of non-metals. They used cause-and-effect reasoning, especially when explaining why nitrogen is used in snack packets and how oxygen supports breathing and burning. The everyday-use connections were practised through easy questions; a new why or unfamiliar-situation question should be checked next time. At home, ask them to choose three household examples and explain why that non-metal is used.
